title: A Inheritance for the Ledger
premise: True-crime podcaster Dominic Reyes arrives in the fog-bound coastal town of Marrow Bay to cover its coldest case: the 1962 disappearance of founder Elias Thorne, whose body was never found. When the town council exhumed his memorial coffin last spring and discovered it empty, every official record closed—but Dominic's digging reveals a witness, Marguerite 'Rue' Calloway, listed as dead in 1971, who may still be alive and hiding in plain sight among the town's oldest families. As Dominic follows Rue's trail through ledgers, lighthouse logs, and a tide chart that doesn't match the official drowning story, she uncovers that Elias faked his death to escape his partners, and that the town's founding wealth was built on a shipwreck they caused deliberately. The climax comes at the drowned wreck site, where the last living partner's grandson tries to silence Dominic and Rue both; the resolution sees Rue testify at last, the town forced to reckon with its inheritance, and Dominic—once an outsider by choice—choosing to stay as the keeper of the true story.
about_author: Oscar Marchetti is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipwreck records along the Pacific coast before turning to fiction. He writes mysteries about small towns that keep their histories underwater.

chapters.title: The Empty Box
chapters.summary: Dominic Reyes, POV. Arriving in Marrow Bay for her podcast's new season, she attends a town meeting where the exhumation photos circulate: Elias Thorne's coffin, buried with honors in 1962, contains only ballast stones. The town wants silence; Dominic smells a season-long story. Emotional beat: the thrill of a door opening where everyone else sees a wall.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. In the historical society's basement she finds Thorne's business ledger, its final pages torn out, and a marginal note referencing a payment to someone named only 'R.C.' The archivist, an elderly woman named Ida, warns her gently that some debts were paid in other currencies. Emotional beat: first unease—the town's warmth has edges.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She Drowned
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. She tracks the 1971 obituary of Marguerite Calloway, Thorne's bookkeeper, drowned off the jetty—yet the coroner's file lists no body recovered. A retired deputy admits off-record that the funeral was closed-casket. Emotional beat: the cold-case itch sharpening into certainty that someone was erased on purpose.

chapters.title: The Tide Chart Lie
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Cross-referencing tide tables against the official drowning report, she finds the water was too shallow at the stated hour for a body to be swept out. Someone altered the record—or wrote it without looking at the sea. Emotional beat: quiet triumph of method over myth.

chapters.title: Salt in the Walls
chapters.summary: Ida, POV. The archivist remembers being a girl when Rue Calloway vanished from town gossip, and recalls her grandmother burning letters the night the obituary ran. Ida chooses, for the first time in fifty years, to leave a basement drawer unlocked for Dominic. Emotional beat: complicity curdling into courage.

chapters.title: Thorne & Partners
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Researching the shipping firm, she learns Thorne had two partners, the Voss brothers, whose descendants still own half the waterfront. One brother died at sea in 1959; the other built the cannery empire. Emotional beat: realizing the mystery isn't one man's vanishing but a fortune's origin.

chapters.title: A Woman at the Window
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Following a tip about an elderly recluse up the headland, she glimpses a woman sorting through what look like old shipping documents before a curtain falls. The house is registered to a trust older than Dominic's career. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as paranoia.

chapters.title: What the Lighthouse Kept
chapters.summary: Lighthouse keeper's log, 1962, presented through Dominic reading it aloud. Entries describe a boat leaving the cove the night Thorne 'died'—and returning empty, piloted by a man who paid the keeper to skip a page. Emotional beat: history speaking directly, chillingly.

chapters.title: The Grandson
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. She interviews Julian Voss, charming third-generation cannery owner, who laughs off her questions and then, at the door, quietly tells her some inheritances come with obligations attached. That night her rental car's tires are slashed. Emotional beat: the story turning personal and dangerous.

chapters.title: Dead Women Don't Buy Groceries
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. A pharmacy receipt in the trust's name leads her to a delivery service serving the headland house. The driver describes his customer: elderly, sharp, left-handed—matching Rue Calloway's handwriting samples. Emotional beat: proof crystallizing; the dead woman is alive.

chapters.title: Ida's Confession
chapters.summary: Ida, POV. She finally tells Dominic what her family knew: the Vosses paid half the town's founders to forget, and her grandmother took the money out of fear, not greed. She hands over the burned letters' surviving fragments. Emotional beat: grief for a town that sold its soul to belong.

chapters.title: The Wreck Beneath the Ledger
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Deciphering the ledger fragments, she reconstructs the truth: the Vosses deliberately sank a rival's ship in 1958, Thorne helped falsify the insurance, then threatened to confess—which is why he had to die, or vanish. Emotional beat: horror at how neatly crime and commerce interlock.

chapters.title: Knocking on a Dead Woman's Door
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. She climbs to the headland house and confronts the recluse. The woman denies nothing and nothing confirms: 'You have the wrong grave,' she says, in a voice Dominic swears she'll prove belongs to Rue. Emotional beat: two stubborn women measuring each other across fifty years of silence.

chapters.title: Why She Stayed Dead
chapters.summary: Rue, POV (first time). Flashback to 1971: Rue saw the Vosses' men follow Thorne onto the water, testified to no one because no one would listen, and let the town bury her name to survive. She has kept Thorne's real confession hidden ever since, waiting for someone worth the risk. Emotional beat: the weight of surviving by disappearing.

chapters.title: Publish or Perish
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. She drafts the episode revealing everything, then hesitates—airing it exposes Rue and torches Ida's family. Julian Voss makes a generous offer: fund the podcast, soften the story. Dominic declines and finds her lodging reservation mysteriously cancelled. Emotional beat: the cost of integrity made concrete.

chapters.title: The Page the Keeper Skipped
chapters.summary: Dominic and Ida, alternating. They locate the lighthouse keeper's descendants and recover the missing log page: it names the boat, the night, and the man who paid—Julian's grandfather. The evidence chain is complete except for a living witness. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by dread of what completion invites.

chapters.title: What the Tide Took
chapters.summary: Rue, POV. Rue decides to give Dominic Thorne's confession, but insists on delivering it herself—at the wreck site, where the sea can be witness. Meanwhile Julian learns of the log page and makes a call. Emotional beat: resolve hardening even as danger closes.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. At the cove at dawn, Julian confronts them, desperate—not evil, but bound by the obligation he named. He tries to take the confession; a struggle; the papers nearly go into the sea before Ida arrives with the sheriff, whom she has finally chosen over her town. Emotional beat: the climax—loyalties declared at gunpoint of legacy.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Rue, POV. In the county courthouse, Marguerite Calloway gives her statement after fifty-three years legally dead. Her voice steadies as she names the Vosses' crime and Thorne's flight. Julian, facing ruin, surprises everyone by corroborating the ledger evidence his grandfather left him. Emotional beat: catharsis—the witness everyone swore was dead, alive and heard.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. The town holds a second funeral for Elias Thorne—still no body, but now an honest stone. Some residents rage at Dominic; others thank her. The episode airs and downloads explode, yet she finds herself lingering in Marrow Bay past any professional reason. Emotional beat: a reckoning that costs and heals at once.

chapters.title: The Inheritance
chapters.summary: Rue, POV. Rue, dying and unburdened, formally leaves her archive—Thorne's confession, her own journals—to Dominic rather than the town that erased her. 'You stayed invisible to stay safe,' she tells her. 'I'm asking you to be visible instead.' Emotional beat: found family sealed in paper and trust.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Story
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV. Months later, Dominic signs a lease above the historical society, co-curating a truthful exhibit with Ida while recording season two: not cold cases, but the people who survived them. The tide comes in clean over the cove. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited—and finally enough.
